summary: Mihai Eminescu worked in Indology and other fields. He studied at Staatsgymnasium Czernowitz, the University of Vienna (1869–1872), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1872–1874) under Albrecht Weber.

Mihai Șora was a philosopher who studied at the University of Bucharest (~1934–1938) under Mircea Eliade, the University of Paris (~1939–1945), and the CNRS (~1945–1948). He held a post at the State Publishing House for Literature and Arts (~1959–1969).
Mihail Alekseevič Širjaev was an Indologist who studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy and Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov. He served as Docent of Indology at Leningrad Oriental Institute.

Mihail Nikolaevič Sotnikov worked in Indology and linguistics. He held posts as Docent of Indology at Leningrad Oriental Institute, Head of Department of Indian Linguistics at MGIMO (1954–1956), and at Moscow State University (1956–1965).
Mikael Aktor specializes in religious studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Copenhagen in 1998 and became an Associate Professor at the University of Southern Denmark in 1999.

Mikaël Bauer works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Kanazawa University under Paul Hoornaert and Noritoshi Aramaki, and earned a PhD from Harvard under Ryuichi Abe (attested 2010). He is attested as Associate Professor at McGill University in 2026.

Mikel Burley works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Essex under J. M. Bernstein, studied under Jonardon Ganeri and Brian Carr, and completed his PhD at Bristol (-2005) under John Peacock. He is an Associate Professor at Leeds.

Mikhail Tubyansky was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Theodore Stcherbatsky and Boris Vladimirtsov. From 1920 to 1937 he held posts at the Asiatic Museum, IOM RAS, and Leningrad Institute of Living Oriental Languages.

Mikhail Kudryavtsev was an Indologist who studied at Leningrad Topographical Technical School (1929–1932) and Saint Petersburg State University (~1934–1939). He worked at the Institute of Ethnography as a naučnyj sotrudnik in 1948 and staršij naučnyj sotrudnik in 1969.

Mikhail Peterson worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Moscow State University (~1908–1913) under Wiktor Jan Porzeziński, Filipp Fedorovich Fortunatov, and Nikolai Trubetzkoy, later serving there as Docent from 1916 to 1952.
Mikhail Pokrovsky studied under Vsevolod Miller and Filipp Fedorovich Fortunatov from circa 1887 to 1891.

Mikhail Sergeevich Troitsky worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts of the Russian Academy of Sciences (1928–1931) and held a post at the University of Chicago.
Mikhaïl Peterson studied under Wiktor Jan Porzeziński and Filipp Fedorovich Fortunatov (~1909–1913) and later taught Pavel Grintser and Vyacheslav Ivanov.
Mikio Otsuki works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. In 2007, he is attested as a research fellow at Manpuku-ji and as a professor at Hanazono University.

Mikisaburo Mori was a philosopher and Sinologist. He studied at Kyoto University and Osaka University, and held teaching posts at Kyoto University, Osaka High School, Osaka University (1950, 1966–1973), and Bukkyo University (~1973–1980).

Mikołaj Kruszewski was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Warsaw and Kazan State University under Jan Niecisław Baudouin de Courtenay. He held several posts at Kazan State University from 1879, becoming Professor in 1885.

Mikołaj Rudnicki worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Jan Michał Rozwadowski at Jagiellonian University (~1903–1911) and served as Professor of Indo-European Linguistics at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań (1919–1950).

Mildred Archer was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who earned degrees at St Hilda's College, Oxford (~1931–1977). She served as Keeper of Printings and Drawings at the India Office from 1954 to 1980.

Milena Hübschmannová was an Indologist and linguist who earned her PhD at Charles University. She held posts at the Oriental Institute and Czech Academy of Sciences, and became Professor of Romani at Charles University in 1991.

Miles Bronson was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Colgate University (~1832–1834) and Colgate Rochester Crozer Divinity School (~1834–1836). He founded the American Baptist Missionary Union in 1837.
